title: 2025-06-11-poc-weekly-bootstrap-access-benchmarks
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on onboarding status, AWS access and VPC peering, initial perf numbers from sandbox runs, and next steps for a controlled benchmark. Security questions around KMS and audit logs were raised; Redwood agreed to provide docs and a short test harness. Action items assigned for granting access and running a 24-hour soak test.
next_steps: Redwood: Share sandbox runbook and synthetic load script (Alex) - by 2025-06-13
Customer: Grant cross-account role and S3 read-only for pilot bucket - Maya - by 2025-06-14
Redwood SE to schedule 2-hour benchmark window next week - Priya - propose times by 2025-06-12
Customer Sec to review KMS docs and confirm key policies - Omar - by 2025-06-16
action_items: Alex Rivera - Send sandbox quickstart, upload sample prompts and bench script - due 2025-06-13
Maya Patel - Provision cross-account role 'redwood-pilot' and confirm VPC peering CIDR - due 2025-06-14
Priya Shah - Prepare baseline perf dashboard (p50/p95, cold vs warm) and instrumentation notes - due 2025-06-12
Omar Ruiz - Provide list of compliance checkpoints for SOC2 gap analysis - due 2025-06-16
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - Alex from Redwood, Priya our SE, Ben joining for CSM. Customer team?
[00:08] Jordan (Customer): Jordan here, Maya, Omar, Leah on my side.
[00:12] Priya (SE): Great, we'll keep this tight, 45 minutes. Agenda: access status, early sandbox runs, security questions, and schedule for a controlled benchmark.
[00:25] Maya: On access - I tried the cross-account role earlier, had a permission error on the STS assume role step. It said invalid principal? Also the V-PC peering template the console gave looks like it has overlapping CIDR with our prod account, so we paused.
[00:38] Alex: OK, thanks. The role we asked you to create is 'redwood-pilot-role' with just sts:AssumeRole and S3 read for the pilot bucket, is that what you created?
[00:45] Maya: I think so, but I may have used an existing trust policy which pointed to the wrong account ID. We'll correct that. Also, can you confirm minimum IAM permissions for the pilot? We prefer least privilege.
[00:52] Priya: Yes, we'll send a pared-down policy. It really only needs sts:AssumeRole, s3:GetObject for the pilot bucket, and cloudwatch:PutMetricData optionally if you want our agent to push traces. No EC2 admin rights.
[01:03] Jordan: Cool. On the sandbox runs you did — can you summarize the numbers? We ran a quick smoke yesterday.
[01:10] Priya: Sure. On the hosted sandbox we saw median generation latency around 72ms for 256-token prompts after warmups; cold starts up to ~240-280ms per request depending on KV cache warm state. Throughput was about 40 requests/sec with a continuous batch size averaging 4. These are rough numbers; the sample prompt set was lighter than your production distribution.
[01:30] Jordan: That matches roughly what we saw. Our production prompt median is more like 512 tokens so we expect higher. Did you test quantized variants?
[01:38] Priya: We did int8 for the LLM slice — gave us about 20-25% cost drop with a small bump in p95 latency. For int4 it's promising but requires more tuning; sometimes there's a higher tail for long contexts. Also, we tried enabling prefix cache — that knocked about 30% off cost on repeated prefixes but only if the prefix hit rate is high.
[01:55] Maya: You mentioned "KV cash" in the notes, is that KV cache?
[01:58] Priya: Yes, sorry, KV cache. The auto-prefix/KV cache is important for dialogue workloads.
[02:03] Omar (Security): Quick security question: what's your KMS pattern? Do you require customer-managed keys for the pilot or is Redwood's key acceptable for hosted? Also audit logs — what retention and format?
[02:14] Alex: For hosted pilots we default to Redwood-managed keys but for enterprise pilots you can bring your own (CMK). We'll send the KMS integration doc. Audit logs are available via the console and we can push to an S3 bucket or CloudWatch; retention is configurable but we'll share our retention defaults and available exports.
[02:30] Omar: And SSO? We use Okta SAML. We'll need a SAML integration for console access and role mapping.
[02:36] Ben (CSM): We can configure SAML to map to RBAC roles for the pilot; we do a scoped-admin role for SEs and an observer for the customer.
[02:43] Leah (Product): On success criteria — we need <150ms median for 256 tokens and less than 300ms p95 for our baseline feature. Is that an achievable target with your config?
[02:52] Priya: In the hosted sandbox we hit ~72ms median for 256 tokens after warm. So yes median is easily achievable; p95 depends on cold starts and long context tails. With prefix caching and a small dedicated pool or reserved concurrency we can hit your p95 target. If you need hard SLOs we'd recommend Redwood Dedicated or a reserved capacity path.
[03:13] Jordan: Cost is a concern too. What's the unit economics you're seeing on the quantized models?
[03:19] Priya: Roughly, int8 gives ~20% cost savings vs fp16; combined with batching and auto-prefix caching you can get an additional 15-30% depending on hit rates. We also provide model recommendations in the dashboard for cost vs quality tradeoffs.
[03:33] Maya: We had an issue with NAT and the peering route tables — traffic to the Redwood endpoint was returning a 403 on initial tests; likely our egress restriction. Any recommended networking checklist?
[03:42] Alex: We'll send a VPC peering checklist. Key items: allow outbound to Redwood endpoint IPs, ensure route tables include the peer, check security group egress and NACLs, and make sure STS endpoints are reachable. We'll include common troubleshooting steps.
[03:54] Jordan: For the benchmark next week — what's the minimal test we should run to validate both latency and cost?
[04:00] Priya: We recommend a two-phase run: a 1-hour warm-up at target QPS to populate KV/prefix cache and a 2-hour steady-state bench. Use a realistic prompt distribution (we'll provide sample prompt sets) including variance in token lengths. Capture p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and cost per 1k tokens. Also run a cold-start burst test to measure tail behavior.
[04:22] Maya: How do we enable logging so we can correlate traces with our app logs?
[04:26] Priya: We support trace ids in response headers and structured logs that can be forwarded to your SIEM. If you give our agent CloudWatch PutMetricData permission we can push metrics; otherwise we can push to S3 for you to ingest.
[04:37] Omar: Any red flags for compliance in the sandbox? We won't use real PII but want to know if data residency is enforced.
[04:44] Alex: For hosted sandbox it's multi-tenant and not suitable for regulated data. For pilot with customer-managed key and private deployment (VPC option) you can get isolation. We'll send a matrix that outlines which features are gated for each deployment mode.
[04:58] Jordan: OK, final recap so we're aligned?
[05:01] Ben: I'll recap: Redwood to share sandbox runbook, VPC peering checklist, KMS and audit log docs, and bench script. Customer to provision cross-account role and confirm peering CIDRs. SE to propose two 2-hour windows for benchmark next week. Security to review KMS docs.
[05:18] Maya: Sounds good. I'll get the role and let you know when it's ready.
[05:21] Alex: Great — we'll follow up via email with the links and runbook. Thanks everyone.
[05:26] Jordan: Thanks all.
[05:28] (call ends)
